profile.campus: Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia (Equinix DC7, Washington DC-area IBX network)
profile.address: 7990 Science Applications Ct, Suite 1, Vienna, VA 22180
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's DC7 "Washington DC IBX" facility on Quantum Drive/Science Applications Court in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia, which Equinix's own site describes as serving as a major communications gateway to Europe given the Washington DC region's strategic importance for transatlantic network routes. DC7 is part of Equinix's wider Northern Virginia footprint, anchored by the much larger Ashburn "Data Center Alley" campus in neighboring Loudoun County, where Equinix's first buildings, DC1 and DC2, were established in the late 1990s. Equinix's published material for DC7 confirms N+1 electrical and cooling redundancy and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, and SOC 2 Type II, describing the site as home to a high concentration of network, cloud, and IT service providers, alongside amenities like conference rooms and WiFi for colocation customers. Equinix's public DC7 page did not disclose the building's exact square footage, power capacity, or opening date in the material fetched this session, reserving detailed facility specifications for a downloadable spec sheet rather than the public page; this registry declines to estimate those figures rather than adopting an unconfirmed aggregator number. DC7 offers colocation, private cages, smart-hands support, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and Equinix's Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products, consistent with the rest of the Washington DC-area Equinix IBX network.

Dominion Energy, the regional utility serving most of Northern Virginia including Vienna and the broader Fairfax County data center corridor, has cited data center and other large-load growth as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, underscoring why Equinix's "major communications gateway to Europe" framing for DC7 sits within a regional power and connectivity market under sustained growth pressure.

reading.body:
Equinix DC7 is a colocation facility in Vienna, Fairfax County, serving as part of the Washington DC-area IBX network, which Equinix describes as a major transatlantic communications gateway to Europe. The facility offers standard colocation services including private cages, cross-connects, internet exchange access, and Equinix's Fabric interconnection products. DC7 holds certifications for HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, and SOC 2 Type II, qualifying it to serve regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government. Equinix has not published the power capacity, square footage, or opening date of DC7 in its public materials.

DC7's power capacity is not disclosed, so its size relative to AI infrastructure cannot be determined from published sources. The facility sits within Northern Virginia's data center corridor, anchored by Equinix's much larger Ashburn campus in neighboring Loudoun County. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has identified data center growth as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory, placing sustained pressure on the regional grid.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. DC7 does not appear among those 23 published-capacity facilities. Without published power specifications, this facility cannot be ranked or assessed as a constraint on AI scaling in the state or region.
